notes.meaning: A good name means a godly reputation and upright character, which is far more valuable than costly perfume or earthly luxury. For someone who lives faithfully, the day of death is better than the day of birth because it brings an end to earthly trouble and ushers the soul into rest with God. Birth enters a world of sorrow, but a faithful death finishes the race well.

differ.view: Some Baptists emphasize that the death mentioned here includes the passing of loved ones, which teaches the living to soberly consider their own short time on earth and live with eternity in view.
Reformed writers teach that the day of death acts like God's megaphone to wake our souls up to the fragility of life and direct our focus entirely to His sovereign care.

notes.meaning: Visiting a funeral or comforting a grieving family does the soul more good than attending noisy parties. A funeral reminds every living person of the unavoidable end awaiting everyone on earth. Facing this reality nudges people to examine their lives and turn their hearts toward God.

Sober sorrow has greater spiritual value than empty jokes and thoughtless laughter. A somber face often reflects a softened heart that is learning humility, repenting of wrong, and growing in wisdom. Hard times can cleanse the inner life far more deeply than shallow amusement ever could.

Wise people choose to reflect on serious matters like death, grief, and eternity. Fools, on the other hand, spend their energies chasing lighthearted amusements and continuous partying. By avoiding reality, the foolish never grow in true spiritual understanding.

Hearing honest correction from a wise friend may sting, but it brings health and life to the spirit. Listening to the flattering songs and empty chatter of fools might feel nice for a moment, but it damages the soul. A sensible person welcomes loving reproof over harmful praise.

The loud laughter of fools is like dry brushwood burning under a cooking pot. It makes a noisy crackle and a sudden bright flame, but it dies out quickly without producing real warmth or cooking the meal. Shallow worldly mirth is hollow and cannot satisfy.

Cruel oppression can push even a sensible person into frantic, reckless behavior. Taking a bribe is just as destructive, blinding a person's moral sense and corrupting their understanding. Unfair power and dishonest gain tear down genuine wisdom.

The outcome of a matter reveals its true value far better than its uncertain start. A patient spirit quietly trusts God through trials to see how things turn out, whereas a proud spirit demands quick results and easily loses control. Humility breeds the patience needed to finish well.

People should not be quick-tempered or harbor resentment when offended. While anger may briefly cross the mind of a wise person, it makes a lasting home only in the chest of a fool. Nursing grievances robs a person of peace and leads to foolish actions.

Constantly claiming that the past was better than the present shows a lack of wisdom. Every generation has faced trials and hardships, and God's mercies are just as real today as they were long ago. Complaining about the times often hides a discontented heart that questions God's providence.

Wisdom is an excellent treasure, especially when paired with an inherited estate. Wealth alone can be squandered, but when guided by wisdom, it becomes a powerful tool to do good for the living. True understanding turns material blessings into lasting benefits.

Both money and wisdom offer shelter and protection from many hardships in life. Yet wisdom possesses a clear advantage because it guards and preserves the inner and spiritual life of its owner. Riches may be lost or bring danger, but godly understanding leads to eternal safety.

People ought to ponder the sovereign deeds of God and humbly accept what He brings to pass. No human being can straighten or alter what God has appointed to be difficult or crooked. Recognizing our limits silences our complaints against His ruling hand.

When good days arrive, people should enjoy them with gratitude to God. When difficult days come, they should reflect on God's sovereignty, knowing He weaves both comfort and trouble into life. God orders life this way so people realize they cannot control the future and must depend wholly on Him.

In this broken world, life does not always seem fair. An upright person sometimes dies young or suffers persecution for doing what is right, while a wicked person may enjoy a long and comfortable life. Observing these confusing situations reminds believers to trust God beyond outward appearances.

This warning cautions against proud self-righteousness and rigid, pushy behavior. Putting on an air of superior wisdom and meddling harshly in everything can bring unnecessary trouble and ruin upon a person. True godliness is marked by humble obedience rather than legalistic display.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars translate the final word as being 'astonished' or 'confounded,' suggesting the verse describes a person becoming bewildered when rigid piety fails to protect them from life's unfair hardships.

notes.meaning: Sinners must not think that because the wicked sometimes live long, they can abandon all restraint. Diving headlong into reckless, ungodly living invites sudden harm and can cut a person's life short. Fools destroy themselves by provoking both human justice and the judgment of God.

It is vital to hold firmly to both warnings, steering clear of both self-righteous pride and reckless ungodliness. The person who genuinely reveres God will walk a straight, steady path and escape these destructive extremes. True reverence before God keeps a believer balanced and safe.

Godly wisdom provides greater strength and security than ten powerful rulers defending a fortress. Military might and political power can easily fail, but sound judgment protects a person's spirit through life's trials. Wisdom is a quiet yet mighty shield.

Every human being on earth falls short of perfection, and even the most righteous stumble into sin. No one consistently does good without ever failing in word, thought, or action. Recognizing this universal weakness keeps believers humble and reliant on God's mercy.

A person should not eavesdrop or obsess over every word whispered by others, or they will inevitably hear a servant or friend speaking ill of them. Conscience quickly reminds us that we too have often spoken unkindly or critically about other people. Remembering our own slip-ups helps us overlook the faults and careless remarks of others.

Even with deep study and great abilities, the Preacher discovered that total, exhaustive wisdom was beyond human grasp. God's providences and the ultimate reasons behind all things are profoundly deep and far out of reach. Honest reflection forces people to admit how small their knowledge really is.

The writer set his entire heart on exploring the true nature of wisdom and discovering why things happen as they do. He was equally determined to understand the inner workings of foolishness, rebellion, and moral madness. Sin is not just a minor slip; it is a dangerous spiritual madness.

Of all traps in life, a seductive and deceptive person is more bitter and deadly than death itself. Her flattering words and charms are like nets, and her embrace acts like prison chains. Only by God's gracious help does someone walk away safely, while those who wander in sin get caught in her grip.

Examining his observations one by one, the Preacher noted how exceptionally rare true, steadfast godliness is in fallen humanity. Out of a thousand people, he found barely one truly upright man, and among his royal harem of foreign wives, not a single one proved faithful. His sorrowful findings reflect the terrible damage of widespread moral decline and unrestrained living.

The ultimate lesson learned is that God created humanity upright, innocent, and properly ordered toward Him. Human beings, however, broke away from God's good design and invented countless schemes and rebellious paths. All our misery and confusion flow not from God's creation, but from human rebellion against Him.
